steps: Hold both hands in front of your chest in loose, relaxed 5-handshapes with your fingers slightly bent.
Angle both hands forward and slightly downward, with the fingertips pointing out and down.
Pump both hands forward and down, then back up, in a small repeated bouncing motion.
Keep your palms angled forward and down for the whole movement.
Use a relaxed, casual mouth shape, since chatting is informal, easy conversation.
tip: One-handed and two-handed loose-C versions also exist, but the two-handed 5-hand bounce is the most common.

steps: Make a fist with your non-dominant hand and hold it out in front of your torso, knuckles up.
Open your dominant hand flat with the fingers held together, palm facing down.
Sweep the flat hand forward across the top of the fist in one smooth, firm pass away from your body.
tip: ENOUGH mirrors FULL: FULL glides the flat hand backward over the fist, while ENOUGH glides it forward.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand open and flat in front of you, palm facing up like a page of paper.
Touch the tip of your dominant index finger to the dip of your dominant thumb, as if holding a pen.
Scribble quickly across the open palm with small side-to-side strokes, as if writing a note.
Keep your dominant palm facing down or slightly toward you while you scribble.
Hold the non-dominant hand steady; it does not move while the other hand writes.
tip: For 'wrote a paper' use one quick downward stroke; for 'write your name' use one careful sideways stroke.

steps: Extend both index fingers and hold your hands out in front of your torso, fingers pointing straight forward.
Curl the other fingers down into your palms and angle your palms slightly downward.
Flick both index fingers upward in one quick, sharp snapping motion.
Keep the movement brisk and short, ending with the fingertips pointing up.
tip: A related snap with the thumbs tucked between the fingers means 'fast' or 'immediately' instead.

steps: Open your dominant hand into a 5-handshape with all fingers spread.
Hold the hand beside your face at cheek height, palm facing back toward your own face.
Draw one full circle around your face in the air, keeping the hand open the whole time.
Keep the palm facing back toward you as it circles.
tip: The 5-hand version means looks or appearance; tracing the circle with just an index finger simply means a face.

steps: Fingerspell O-I-L with your dominant hand, holding it at shoulder height.
Flow the three letters together smoothly and quickly, without pausing between them.
Keep your palm angled forward toward your conversation partner as you spell.
Keep the movement compact and relaxed, the way Deaf signers blend common fingerspelled words.
tip: OIL is a lexicalized fingerspelling: Deaf signers spell it fast as one blended unit rather than three separate letters.

steps: Bring your dominant thumb and fingertips together so they nearly touch, leaving only a tiny gap.
Hold the pinched hand up in front of your chest at a comfortable height.
Angle your palm inward toward yourself and give the pinch a tiny wiggle to show the small amount.
tip: The smaller the gap between thumb and fingertips, the smaller the amount you are describing.

steps: Form both hands into H-handshapes, index and middle fingers extended together and pointing sideways.
Hold both hands close together in the signing space in front of your chest.
Turn your non-dominant palm down and your dominant palm up to start.
Move the dominant hand up and then down onto the non-dominant fingers, ending with the dominant palm facing down.
tip: Puff your cheeks slightly while signing INCREASE to mean gaining weight; keep a neutral face for a raise or a rising price.

steps: Close both hands into fists and bring them together in front of your chest, one stacked on the other.
Place the dominant fist on top of the non-dominant fist so the knuckles touch.
Twist both wrists together at the same time, as if screwing two pieces into place.
Keep both palms facing inward toward each other through the twist.
Use a focused, deliberate expression, as if building or forming something.
tip: ASL shows past time with a time sign like BEFORE or PAST, so 'created' is this same MAKE movement plus the time marker.

steps: Form a K-handshape with your dominant hand: index finger pointing straight up, middle finger bent down.
Hold the hand beside your forehead, with the middle-finger tip close to your temple.
Trace a small circle in the air beside your temple.
Finish the circle by touching the tip of your middle finger to your forehead.
tip: POLITICAL is GOVERNMENT initialized with a P/K handshape: same temple circle, different fingers.
